correctness.rationale: The orbit graph of a tree under an automorphism subgroup is a forest by rooting the barycentric subdivision at the invariant center; for disjoint components reduce to setwise stabilizers. Fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on orbits. A set of orbits in the fixed-point simplex excludes full closed neighborhoods precisely when its orbit support forms a face of Dom(Q); orbit barycenters yield a PL homeomorphism. The established Marietti–Testa forest dominance sphere formula yields dimension ν(Q)−1, empty when ν=0; reduced Lefschetz equality yields sign (−1)^(ν(F)−ν(Q_<g>)) on rank-one integral top homology. Cases of empty fixed complexes and isolated vertices use augmented reduced Euler conventions; non-equivariant theorem is credited as preexisting.
